parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a matte black anodized aluminum rod bent into a loop.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing surface for clipping onto ropes or gear.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper can securely grasp the straight spine section of the loop from the side.
physics.reason: Carabiner bodies are typically forged or machined from solid metal stock to withstand high tensile loads.

parts.description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a matte black anodized aluminum rod bent into a loop.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing surface for clipping onto ropes or gear.

parts.name: nose lug

physics.Basic_description: A small protruding block at the tip of the carabiner body, matching the black anodized finish of the main loop.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the catch point where the wire gate rests to close the loop securely.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integral to the body to be grasped independently; would be avoided during manipulation.
physics.reason: This is a machined feature of the solid main body forging.

parts.description: A small protruding block at the tip of the carabiner body, matching the black anodized finish of the main loop.
parts.function: Acts as the catch point where the wire gate rests to close the loop securely.

parts.name: wire loop

physics.Basic_description: A thin, dark grey metal wire bent into a rectangular loop shape that forms the gate.
physics.Functional_description: Springs open to allow clipping and snaps shut to secure the connection, lighter than solid gates to reduce flutter.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be pinched by fine-tipped grippers to depress the gate, though it is flexible and thin.
physics.reason: Wire gates are formed from solid round or oval steel wire stock.

parts.description: A thin, dark grey metal wire bent into a rectangular loop shape that forms the gate.
parts.function: Springs open to allow clipping and snaps shut to secure the connection, lighter than solid gates to reduce flutter.

parts.name: wire hinge plate

physics.Basic_description: A tiny metallic segment at the base of the wire gate where it pivots.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the wire gate to the body hinge pin, allowing rotational movement.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp; located at the pivot point which should be avoided to prevent damage.
physics.reason: Part of the solid wire assembly or a small solid ferrule.

parts.description: A tiny metallic segment at the base of the wire gate where it pivots.
parts.function: Secures the wire gate to the body hinge pin, allowing rotational movement.

parts.name: wire latch tip

physics.Basic_description: The very end of the wire gate, appearing as a small rounded tip.
physics.Functional_description: Interfaces with the nose lug to complete the closure of the carabiner.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small for independent grasping; usually contacted only when depressing the gate.
physics.reason: Formed from the solid end of the wire stock.

parts.description: The very end of the wire gate, appearing as a small rounded tip.
parts.function: Interfaces with the nose lug to complete the closure of the carabiner.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A small cylindrical pin visible at the hinge junction, likely steel.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the axle for the wire gate to rotate around.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; it is a small mechanical fastener embedded in the assembly.
physics.reason: Pins are solid cylinders of metal designed to resist shear forces.

parts.function: Acts as the axle for the wire gate to rotate around.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
